title: tests do not pin the tenant source on the WRITE routes: mutating guarded() to take the tenant from an x-tenant-id request header, and mutating the approvals route to take it from a body field, both leave router.test.ts (13/13) and the real-store round trip (4/4) green
evidence: Checker mutation run on dd11749 (per-mutation byte backup, hash restored to HEAD blob b6d70720676d6c250a5d80ef45411234de6cabac). M1: router.ts guarded() `const tenantId = req.auth!.tenantId;` -> `const tenantId = String(req.header("x-tenant-id") ?? req.auth!.tenantId);` => router.test.ts pass 13 fail 0; scripts/qa pass 4 fail 0 (SURVIVED). M8: approvals handler takes `req.body.tenant` as the tenant when present (bodyOf allow-list widened to include it) => 13/13 and 4/4 (SURVIVED). The production code is correct today (checker probe: tenant-b key sending x-tenant-id/x-tenant/tenant-id/x-forwarded-tenant: tenant-a and ?tenantId=tenant-a on GET returned B's own empty rules; PUT/approval bodies with tenantId/tenant/state/constructor/__proto__ got 400; tenant-a bytes unchanged), but no test sends a hostile tenant hint on any write route, so a regression that re-routes writes to another tenant ships green. Mutations M2 (opt-outs without requireScope), M3 (PUT without load-first), M4 (no mutex), M5 (no validation), M6 (poisoned queue), M7 (GET without requireScope) were all killed.
fix_direction: Add to router.test.ts (and ideally the real-store test): with a tenant-b key, send PUT/POST approvals/POST opt-outs/GET carrying x-tenant-id, x-tenant, tenant-id, ?tenantId= and body fields tenantId/tenant (top level and nested) naming tenant-a; assert tenant-a's stored value is byte-identical afterwards and any write landed (if at all) only under tenant-b. Re-run mutations M1 and M8 and report both killed.
reproduction: 1) cp apps/api/src/join-rules/router.ts to a byte backup. 2) In guarded() replace `const tenantId = req.auth!.tenantId;` with `const tenantId = String(req.header("x-tenant-id") ?? req.auth!.tenantId);`. 3) cd apps/api && node --test --import tsx src/join-rules/router.test.ts => pass 13 fail 0. 4) node --test --import tsx scripts/qa/join-rules-edit-api.test.ts from repo root => pass 4 fail 0. 5) restore and verify git hash-object == git rev-parse HEAD:apps/api/src/join-rules/router.ts.

title: write access to the auto-join rules and approvals is granted by the same `calendar` scope that already guards the read-only GET /calendar/upcoming, so every existing calendar read key silently gains the power to decide which meetings a bot joins with no click
evidence: Probe on dd11749 with a key whose scopes are exactly ["calendar"]: PUT /calendar/join-rules with the allow rule {id:a,effect:allow,match:{platform:meet}} (a rule matching every Meet meeting) => 200; POST /calendar/join-rules/approvals {kind:"domain",value:"gmail.com"} => 200 ACCEPTED (stored in approvedDomains); {kind:"domain",value:"co.uk"} => 200. Scopes are free-form strings (routes/keys.ts accepts any non-empty string array), and sibling mutating routes use a dedicated resource scope (gmail for meeting-candidates approve/reject, sources, ingest, keys, compete). Declared by the maker as a known limit; unwired today (503), so no live exposure yet.
fix_direction: Approver decision before production wiring: require a distinct write scope (for example `calendar:write` or `join-rules`) on PUT and both POST routes, keep `calendar` for GET only, and add per-route 403 tests for a calendar-only key on the writes. Until decided, do not wire joinRules into buildProductionDeps.
reproduction: createServer with keyStore {k: {tenantId:'t1', scopes:['calendar']}} and joinRules wired to the real store; PUT /calendar/join-rules body {version:1,ownDomains:[],rules:[{id:a,effect:allow,match:{platform:meet}}]} with Authorization: Bearer k => 200.
